2-inst.1: New administrations promise a new era and a new beginning before a single policy is enacted.
2-inst.2: Government programs give just enough aid to keep you fed but not secure, grateful but not free.
2-inst.3: Legislation promises affordable care that isn't affordable.
2-inst.4: Election cycles re-engage the disillusioned with fear of the other candidate, not new ideas.
2-inst.5: Dissenting populations are labeled deplorables and extremists to strip them of legitimacy.
2-inst.6: Government agencies revise death tolls downward and seal footage of events citizens witnessed.
2-inst.7: Whistleblowers who stay silent are complicit in the harm, and those who speak up are destroyed.
2-inst.8: Stimulus checks arrive and infrastructure is promised, then delayed, then partially delivered.
2-inst.9: Agencies change metrics to match outcomes, so failure can always be reframed as progress.
2-inst.10: Legislation uses words like "reasonable" whose meaning the institution that wrote it controls.
2-inst.11: Administrations engaged in mass surveillance accuse citizens of being security threats.
2-inst.12: Government agencies that harm citizens sue the whistleblowers who exposed them.
2-inst.13: Each power the government is granted during an emergency becomes the baseline for the next one.
2-inst.14: Nations are cut off through sanctions presented as protection for the sanctioned nation.
2-inst.15: Government pits rural against urban and young against old so the population fights over crumbs.
2-inst.16: Party-aligned media outlets do the attacking so the politician's hands stay clean.
2-inst.17: Entire movements are labeled conspiracy theorists and domestic threats to bypass evaluation.
2-inst.18: Officials at congressional hearings refuse to answer direct questions in public.
2-inst.19: Polls are framed to show popular support for a decision made before the poll was commissioned.
2-inst.20: The state turns wars and disasters into founding myths that bind the population to it.
2-inst.21: Gerrymandered communities learn that hoping feels like a setup for disappointment.
2-inst.22: Emergency curfews and surveillance expansions are presented as temporary measures.
2-inst.23: Officials withhold documents and decide behind closed doors "because the public would panic."
2-inst.24: The political system reduces citizens to party affiliation, flattening them into a binary.
2-inst.25: Governments wave the flag while the veteran starves.
2-inst.26: Corporations purchase policy through lobbying, and politicians deliver it into law.
2-inst.27: Agencies raise threat levels and declare emergencies to justify expanding their own powers.
2-inst.28: Allied nations are abandoned in one policy shift once they no longer serve strategic interests.
2-inst.29: New administrations reverse everything the previous one built while real power stays untouched.
2-inst.30: Agencies point to forms filed and protocols followed even when the outcome was devastating.

2-civ.1: Entire nations are sold the American Dream, which delivers just enough to keep them investing.
2-civ.2: Donor nations send aid to nations they destabilized, because a dependent nation is compliant.
2-civ.3: Each generation is promised that the next war will finally bring peace.
2-civ.4: Nations reactivate nationalism in every crisis, and the unity dissolves once the crisis passes.
2-civ.5: Redlining and voter suppression quietly say some lives count more than others.
2-civ.6: Nations rewrite wars of aggression as liberation and teach those lies in schools as fact.
2-civ.7: Citizens who support the war fund the killing, and citizens who oppose it are labeled traitors.
2-civ.8: Societies grant rights and then erode them, trading hope and despair back and forth.
2-civ.9: Constitutional rights are reinterpreted with each new court, so their meaning is never settled.
2-civ.10: International treaties make commitments that sound binding but have no enforcement mechanisms.
2-civ.11: Empires that destabilized entire regions accuse those regions of instability.
2-civ.12: Colonial powers claim victimhood when formerly colonized nations demand reparations.
2-civ.13: Populations that once would have revolted now shrug because their outrage has been exhausted.
2-civ.14: Party lines divide whole nations so precisely that neighbors cannot speak to each other.
2-civ.15: Superpowers arm both sides of civil wars so no nation can gain enough power to challenge them.
2-civ.16: Empires fund proxy wars and install puppet governments so they never have to officially invade.
2-civ.17: Societies retroactively smear the historical figures who once threatened institutional power.
2-civ.18: Nations ignore petitions and treat movements of millions as if they do not exist.
2-civ.19: Think tanks and lobbying firms manufacture the illusion of a grassroots national consensus.
2-civ.20: Entire civilizations bond to a state that creates their suffering and then offers relief.
2-civ.21: Whole populations conclude "nothing ever changes," the exact state of mind the system needs.
2-civ.22: Allied nations accept foreign military bases on their soil "for their protection."
2-civ.23: The democratic state decides what citizens may eat, say, and know, and what children learn.
2-civ.24: Billions of people are sorted into left or right, red or blue, and managed as voting blocs.
2-civ.25: Nations invoke "manifest destiny" to call the suffering their decisions caused inevitable.
2-civ.26: Central banks control the money supply of entire nations whose people did not elect them.
2-civ.27: Nations start wars on fabricated intelligence while millions of human bodies absorb the cost.
2-civ.28: Indigenous communities are displaced once their land and resources have been extracted.
2-civ.29: One empire replaces another and the flag changes, but the extraction model remains identical.
2-civ.30: Modern states run covert operations through intermediaries that leave no official fingerprint.

3-inst.1: New platforms launch promising to connect the world and give everyone a voice.
3-inst.2: Media outlets offer free news and analysis until the audience cannot function without the feed.
3-inst.3: Platforms promise creators a sustainable living, then the revenue share shrinks.
3-inst.4: Outrage cycles are engineered so that stepping away from the news feels irresponsible.
3-inst.5: Independent journalists are labeled unreliable because they threaten the monopoly on narrative.
3-inst.6: Official narratives reframe events witnessed by millions within hours.
3-inst.7: Journalists who publish what's true risk losing access to the sources that provide the truth.
3-inst.8: News cycles follow catastrophe with heartwarming stories, keeping audiences dysregulated.
3-inst.9: Platforms rewrite guidelines so content that was compliant when posted becomes a violation.
3-inst.10: Major outlets cite "officials familiar with the matter," a source that cannot be verified.
3-inst.11: Platforms that harvest user data blame users for not protecting their own privacy.
3-inst.12: Networks caught broadcasting false information sue the fact-checkers who identified it.
3-inst.13: Platforms took our privacy through a million small terms-of-service agreements.
3-inst.14: Shadow-banning lets dissenting voices keep speaking while nobody can hear them.
3-inst.15: Networks pit left against right while corporate ownership profits from both sides.
3-inst.16: Fact-checkers funded by the entities they should investigate turn the check into a weapon.
3-inst.17: Outlets show a movement's worst elements and repeat its most dismissive label.
3-inst.18: Stories that threaten power simply never get covered, so the event ceases to exist.
3-inst.19: The same talking point appears on six networks in the same hour to create apparent consensus.
3-inst.20: Outlets bond audiences through shared outrage until the network's enemy becomes your enemy.
3-inst.21: Independent journalists learn that challenging mainstream narratives gets their funding pulled.
3-inst.22: Platforms control what discourse is allowed and call it "content moderation" for safety.
3-inst.23: Institutions push media literacy on consumers rather than regulating the producers.
3-inst.24: Media metrics flatten complex human beings into hot takes measured by how many people clicked.
3-inst.25: Outlets frame a child raising money for their own surgery as inspiring rather than indicting.
3-inst.26: Advertising revenue determines which stories get told and which get buried.
3-inst.27: Networks amplify division during election cycles and cultural flashpoints to boost ratings.
3-inst.28: Journalists who challenge editorial direction are quietly let go, and their byline disappears.
3-inst.29: A new platform replaces the old one with the same business model wearing different clothes.
3-inst.30: Outlets that amplify misinformation point to editorial independence and the First Amendment.

3-civ.1: Society grants mass media authority as the guardian of truth based on what it claims to be.
3-civ.2: Civilization moved its commerce, politics, and identity onto platforms it doesn't own.
3-civ.3: Media has promised an informed citizenry for over a century while delivering entertainment.
3-civ.4: Every generation is promised "this is the platform that will finally get it right."
3-civ.5: Whole populations are told they cannot interpret reality without institutional guidance.
3-civ.6: Repetition trains populations to accept narratives that contradict their lived experience.
3-civ.7: The information ecosystem leaves citizens either manipulated by media or uninformed without it.
3-civ.8: Decades of "things are getting better" alternate with decades of "everything is falling apart."
3-civ.9: Whole populations are told that what was accepted science yesterday is misinformation today.
3-civ.10: The label "misinformation" is applied to everything from falsehood to inconvenient truth.
3-civ.11: Decades-old propaganda machines label independent thought as propaganda.
3-civ.12: Institutions that manufactured consent for wars claim to be the victims of public distrust.
3-civ.13: Whole populations know they are being manipulated and then open the app anyway.
3-civ.14: Information silos create parallel civilizations that no longer share a common set of facts.
3-civ.15: Global media empires owned by the same entities fund opposing narratives simultaneously.
3-civ.16: Intelligence agencies place stories through trusted journalists so they arrive as reporting.
3-civ.17: Entire nations are demonized by decades of media until the public sees monsters, not humans.
3-civ.18: Generations grow up without knowing what was done in their name because histories are erased.
3-civ.19: Whole populations consent to wars they didn't choose because the consent was manufactured.
3-civ.20: Entire populations are addicted to the news cycle, trained to scan for threat through a screen.
3-civ.21: Billions accept that "you can't fight the algorithm" out of exhaustion rather than agreement.
3-civ.22: Society elevates certain outlets as "trusted sources" and silences other voices as fringe.
3-civ.23: Much of the population cannot distinguish a news report from an opinion column.
3-civ.24: Algorithms sort humanity into consumer segments by what each person will click on next.
3-civ.25: Society invokes "the marketplace of ideas" while the loudest voices are the best-funded voices.
3-civ.26: Six corporations control approximately ninety percent of everything the Western world reads.
3-civ.27: Whole populations are never given a week without a new threat, scandal, or emergency.
3-civ.28: Local newspapers are shuttered, and the communities built on them are left without a voice.
3-civ.29: Propaganda moved from print to radio to social media, but its function never changed.
3-civ.30: The attention economy insists "we don't control what people see, the algorithm does."

4-inst.1: The university sells you belonging with sunlit quads before it sells you tuition.
4-inst.2: Universities offer aid that reduces the sticker price just enough to make debt feel manageable.
4-inst.3: Universities guarantee career success on brochures while graduate employment rates decline.
4-inst.4: Alumni campaigns use nostalgia to turn graduates' loyalty into a revenue stream.
4-inst.5: Schools in low-income communities are underfunded, labeled failing, and stripped of resources.
4-inst.6: Schools protect the standardized test and pathologize the marginalized students who score low.
4-inst.7: Teachers who teach to the test watch the children's curiosity die.
4-inst.8: Schools hand out honor rolls and awards just unpredictably enough to keep students striving.
4-inst.9: Educators are punished for missing curriculum targets that were moved while they were teaching.
4-inst.10: School policies act "at the administration's discretion," leaving students no appeal.
4-inst.11: Schools that systematically fail students blame parents, communities, and home environments.
4-inst.12: Parents who advocate loudly for their children are labeled difficult and disruptive.
4-inst.13: Schools normalize forcing children to sit motionless for six hours and restricting bathrooms.
4-inst.14: Schools silo disciplines so science never speaks to art and psychology never meets economics.
4-inst.15: Schools are ranked against each other and compete for survival rather than collaborate.
4-inst.16: Accreditation bodies police compliance so no school can deviate from the approved model.
4-inst.17: Montessori and Waldorf schools are dismissed as fringe and academically inferior.
4-inst.18: Bullying complaints are assigned a case number and then disappear into bureaucratic silence.
4-inst.19: School boards offer the appearance of community governance while the curriculum is already set.
4-inst.20: Schools manufacture school spirit through hazing traditions and shared adversity.
4-inst.21: Entire teaching staffs say "the district won't let us" and stop trying to teach differently.
4-inst.22: Mandatory testing is framed as "making sure every child gets an equal education."
4-inst.23: Colleges subject adult learners to testing formats designed for children.
4-inst.24: Schools reward students for producing correct answers on demand rather than for understanding.
4-inst.25: An underfunded school tells a child "you can do anything if you believe in yourself."
4-inst.26: Student loan debt cannot be discharged in bankruptcy, a legalized indentured servitude.
4-inst.27: Every spring, annual testing crises decide school funding and teacher employment.
4-inst.28: Teachers who advocate for students over metrics are quietly non-renewed without explanation.
4-inst.29: Schools replace experienced teachers with cheaper staff who burn out within five years.
4-inst.30: Schools apply vague discipline policies so one student is warned and another expelled.

4-civ.1: An entire society idealizes education as the great equalizer and never asks it to prove itself.
4-civ.2: Society presents free, compulsory public education as its greatest gift to its children.
4-civ.3: Society repeats that education is the great equalizer while inequality deepens every decade.
4-civ.4: Lifelong learning has been repackaged as lifelong tuition with one more certificate always due.
4-civ.5: Society ranks a four-year stamp above ten thousand hours spent mastering a craft.
4-civ.6: Nations teach colonialism as exploration and slavery as economic necessity in history class.
4-civ.7: A whole generation must get the degree and drown in debt, or skip it and drown in exclusion.
4-civ.8: Society parades enough success stories across commencement stages to sustain the degree myth.
4-civ.9: What great-grandparents did with an eighth-grade education now takes sixteen years of school.
4-civ.10: Society never defines whether education should produce citizens or workers, so it never fails.
4-civ.11: A system that mass-produces anxiety and debt blames graduates for not being resilient enough.
4-civ.12: Anyone who critiques the education system publicly is accused of being anti-education.
4-civ.13: Most adults ask "how else would you run a school?" because childhood compliance is normalized.
4-civ.14: Society isolates learning in a building separated from nature, community, work, and the body.
4-civ.15: Nations rank children by PISA scores in a geopolitical competition to produce human capital.
4-civ.16: Employers require degrees to maintain the education economy's customer base.
4-civ.17: Homeschooling and indigenous traditions are delegitimized through legislation and stigma.
4-civ.18: Research showing the educational model harms children sits in journals no policymaker reads.
4-civ.19: The myth of meritocracy makes a whole population blame itself for failing within the system.
4-civ.20: Whole generations defend the system by saying, "We all went through it and we turned out fine."
4-civ.21: Whole populations accept "you can't change the education system" as civilizational law.
4-civ.22: Society frames compulsory education as a gift, which makes the compulsion invisible.
4-civ.23: Sixteen years of being told what to think produce adults looking for the next authority.
4-civ.24: Entire populations define themselves by credentials and treat compassion as a soft skill.
4-civ.25: Society insists any child can succeed by trying hard while outcomes track zip code and income.
4-civ.26: The education-industrial complex generates trillions while producing an indebted generation.
4-civ.27: Corporate-funded think tanks publish alarming reports about failing schools to push charters.
4-civ.28: School systems serving marginalized communities are shuttered and their students bused away.
4-civ.29: For-profit charters replace public schools in the same buildings with new signage.
4-civ.30: Society says the system provided the "opportunity" and the student failed to seize it.

5-inst.1: Hospital billboards promise world-class care with smiling families, not what happens inside.
5-inst.2: Pharmaceutical companies sponsor conferences and fund medical education to tilt prescriptions.
5-inst.3: Insurance companies promise coverage that exists on paper but is buried in preauthorization.
5-inst.4: Screening campaigns that say "early detection saves lives" turn healthy humans into patients.
5-inst.5: Patients whose pain resists easy diagnosis are labeled difficult or drug-seeking.
5-inst.6: Patients who report side effects are told the medication is not causing them.
5-inst.7: Healthcare workers who report a safety concern are labeled troublemakers, so they stay silent.
5-inst.8: Insurance approves a procedure this month and denies it next month, unpredictably.
5-inst.9: Each new edition of the diagnostic manual turns normal human experience into a billing code.
5-inst.10: Pharmaceutical ads say a drug "may help" while legally committing to nothing.
5-inst.11: A medical system that corrupted the food supply tells patients to "eat better, exercise more."
5-inst.12: A hospital sued for malpractice counter-sues the patient and buries the case in legal costs.
5-inst.13: Medicine has turned sadness into depression and childhood energy into ADHD.
5-inst.14: The cardiologist sees the heart and the psychiatrist sees the mind, but nobody sees the human.
5-inst.15: The insurer denies the claim, the hospital demands payment, and the patient has no leverage.
5-inst.16: Nurses and pharmacists enforce protocols they privately disagree with.
5-inst.17: Doctors who speak publicly about pharmaceutical overreach are stripped of hospital privileges.
5-inst.18: Insurance appeals vanish into bureaucratic silence, one filed appeal after another.
5-inst.19: Clinical guidelines are written by panels with financial ties to the industries they benefit.
5-inst.20: Hospitals exploit healthcare workers' belief in healing to extract underpaid labor.
5-inst.21: Healthcare workers learn to say, "I can't give each patient more than twelve minutes."
5-inst.22: Hospitals justify involuntary holds with "we're doing this for your safety."
5-inst.23: Patients were denied access to their own medical records until legislation forced it.
5-inst.24: Doctors who became healers spend their days entering billing codes and fighting insurers.
5-inst.25: The healthcare system tells you to "take charge of your health" while it controls the rest.
5-inst.26: Insurance is tied to employment, so the threat of illness keeps workers in jobs that harm them.
5-inst.27: Disease awareness campaigns that say "ask your doctor about" are advertising, not education.
5-inst.28: Rural hospitals are closed because their populations stopped generating enough margin.
5-inst.29: When a patent expires, the company releases a nearly identical molecule at a higher price.
5-inst.30: The hospital that made the error points to the protocol it followed as its shield.

5-civ.1: Society treats "trust the science" as a demand to stop asking questions about medicine.
5-civ.2: Populations told they have the best healthcare in the world are too grateful to demand better.
5-civ.3: Society has heard "a cure is coming" for decades while chronic disease generates revenue.
5-civ.4: Preventive care turns children into lifelong pharmaceutical customers managed by lab numbers.
5-civ.5: Black women die in childbirth at three times the rate of white women in the same hospitals.
5-civ.6: Society denied the harm of tobacco and opioids until the evidence became overwhelming.
5-civ.7: Whole populations can either pay the medical system or risk dying of something treatable.
5-civ.8: Medical breakthroughs are announced with great fanfare and then priced out of reach or shelved.
5-civ.9: A person who feels vibrant and alive can be told they are unhealthy because of one lab value.
5-civ.10: Medical guidelines say "may be appropriate," so no deviation can ever count as a violation.
5-civ.11: An industry earning trillions from sickness accuses holistic medicine of being dangerous.
5-civ.12: Drug companies caught manipulating clinical trials cast themselves as victims of anti-science.
5-civ.13: Patients who once asked "can you cure this?" now ask "can you help me live with this?"
5-civ.14: Medicine splits the human being into billable parts, each assigned to a different specialist.
5-civ.15: Drug companies fund the research that trains the doctors who prescribe the companies' products.
5-civ.16: Licensing boards strip doctors who recommend nutrition over medication of their licenses.
5-civ.17: Ayurveda and indigenous healing practices are dismissed with a single word: quackery.
5-civ.18: Medicine knows nutrition prevents more disease than medication and still ignores root causes.
5-civ.19: Society labels any question about medical authority as anti-science misinformation.
5-civ.20: Whole populations cannot imagine healing without a prescription because fear binds them.
5-civ.21: Whole populations have learned to say, "I need a doctor to tell me what's wrong."
5-civ.22: Patients who question a treatment plan are called irresponsible because "doctor knows best."
5-civ.23: Society treats "I know my body" as naive and "my doctor knows my body" as wise.
5-civ.24: Whole populations have lost the ability to tell discomfort from danger in their own bodies.
5-civ.25: The phrase "trust the science" sounds like an invitation to evidence but works as a command.
5-civ.26: Medications that cost pennies to manufacture are sold for hundreds of dollars.
5-civ.27: Each health emergency becomes a precedent, and temporary emergency powers become permanent.
5-civ.28: Diseases that primarily affect the global poor receive a fraction of the research funding.
5-civ.29: Each new health paradigm promises to fix the last one while carrying the same business model.
5-civ.30: Drug trials are designed to detect short-term efficacy while long-term harm goes unmonitored.

6-inst.1: Bank commercials show families moving into homes, never the same families five years later.
6-inst.2: Corporations offer on-site childcare so employees cannot leave the company without losing it.
6-inst.3: Companies promise pensions and then go bankrupt before the pensions vest.
6-inst.4: Analysts who failed to predict the crash now call it a "buying opportunity."
6-inst.5: Small businesses crushed by corporate pricing are told "the market decided."
6-inst.6: Economists call inflation "transitory" while the price of groceries doubles.
6-inst.7: Entrepreneurs who take venture capital lose control of the thing they built.
6-inst.8: Stimulus payments arrive just often enough to keep desperation from becoming organized.
6-inst.9: The retirement age moves from sixty to sixty-five to seventy as the finish line keeps receding.
6-inst.10: Corporate earnings calls promise "strong tailwinds" without committing to anything specific.
6-inst.11: Corporations that pay poverty wages accuse their workers of laziness and a lack of work ethic.
6-inst.12: Corporations frame workers who unionize for fair compensation as an attack on the business.
6-inst.13: CEOs earn three hundred times the median worker's salary, and nobody comments.
6-inst.14: The financial system keeps the unbanked and the credit-invisible outside it by design.
6-inst.15: Workers compete for three percent raises while CEO compensation rises three hundred percent.
6-inst.16: Credit agencies control your financial identity with a three-digit number you can't verify.
6-inst.17: Financial whistleblowers who expose fraud are blacklisted from the industry.
6-inst.18: Corporations answer complaints with "your feedback is important to us" and nothing more.
6-inst.19: Shareholder votes let the wealthiest investors decide while small shareholders give legitimacy.
6-inst.20: Company picnics and retirement dinners bond workers to the companies that exploit them.
6-inst.21: Neighborhoods in generational poverty have replaced the hope of upward mobility with survival.
6-inst.22: Consumer protection rules promise to protect you "from your own bad decisions."
6-inst.23: Banks charge interest to eighteen-year-olds who were never taught what interest is.
6-inst.24: Human resource departments calculate the cost of a human being like the cost of a machine.
6-inst.25: Corporations tell underpaid workers, "this isn't just a job, it's a calling."
6-inst.26: Employers that control healthcare, retirement, and childcare recreate the company town.
6-inst.27: Market crashes let institutional investors buy middle-class assets at a discount.
6-inst.28: Mass layoffs are executed the week before pensions vest, ending decades of loyalty in one memo.
6-inst.29: Companies replace twenty-year workers with automation because a machine doesn't call in sick.
6-inst.30: Corporations announce layoffs as "strategic restructuring" and blame market conditions.

6-civ.1: Whole nations idealize capitalism as freedom, so questioning it feels like questioning freedom.
6-civ.2: Development loans to impoverished nations are presented as aid but function as acquisition.
6-civ.3: Trickle-down economics promised for fifty years that wealth at the top would flow downward.
6-civ.4: Every generation is told "this time the system works" and re-enters the same economic model.
6-civ.5: Entire nations are labeled "third world" by the metrics of the nations that colonized them.
6-civ.6: Whole populations are told the economy is "strong" while their wages stagnate.
6-civ.7: The global population cannot withdraw from the economic system that extracts from it.
6-civ.8: Booms and busts cycle across decades, and each recovery restores just enough to stop a revolt.
6-civ.9: Housing, healthcare, and food costs rise faster than income in every decade, by design.
6-civ.10: Economic policy is explained in terms like "quantitative easing" that citizens cannot evaluate.
6-civ.11: Societies built on centuries of extraction and redlining blame the poor for being poor.
6-civ.12: Nations impoverished by Western institutions are accused of corruption for seeking debt relief.
6-civ.13: Society expects a person to carry debt from the age of eighteen until death.
6-civ.14: Sanctions strangle entire economies while the starving are told it's for their own protection.
6-civ.15: Nations race to the bottom on labor protections and tax holidays to win foreign investment.
6-civ.16: The World Bank demands privatization and cuts to social spending as conditions for its loans.
6-civ.17: Critics of capitalism are labeled socialists and discredited before they open their mouths.
6-civ.18: Central banks make decisions behind closed doors that affect billions of human lives.
6-civ.19: The myth of the free market blames human policy choices on market forces no one can vote out.
6-civ.20: People who spent their lives inside capitalism cannot picture a world organized differently.
6-civ.21: Whole populations say "the rich get richer" with the resignation of a weather report.
6-civ.22: Central banks frame control of the money supply as "managing inflation for the common good."
6-civ.23: Society keeps the language of economics deliberately inaccessible to block financial literacy.
6-civ.24: GDP rankings place a miserable but productive country above a joyful but poor one.
6-civ.25: Society credits "the invisible hand of the market" for outcomes that human decisions produced.
6-civ.26: Nations owe more than they can ever repay to institutions that create money from nothing.
6-civ.27: The 2008 collapse erased household wealth while the institutions behind it were bailed out.
6-civ.28: Nations used as commodity sources are left with debt, depleted soil, and polluted water.
6-civ.29: Fiat currency is evolving toward programmable money that can be tracked and frozen.
6-civ.30: Global finance hides extraction behind layers of abstraction so dense that causation is lost.

8-inst.1: The family insists "we're the perfect family" and treats any honest member as the problem.
8-inst.2: Parents say "I gave up my career for you" during conflict, turning the sacrifice into a debt.
8-inst.3: Couples promise to work on the marriage "when the kids are older," a future that never arrives.
8-inst.4: Families say "you're breaking your mother's heart by not coming to Christmas" to pull you back.
8-inst.5: The family makes one child the scapegoat who carries all the blame for its dysfunction.
8-inst.6: The family insists "we had a great childhood" and pathologizes anyone who remembers otherwise.
8-inst.7: Adult children who set a boundary are labeled the one who destroyed the family.
8-inst.8: Parents praise one child last week and criticize them this week, so no child ever feels secure.
8-inst.9: The child who was supposed to be a doctor is suddenly supposed to be a lawyer.
8-inst.10: Families run on unspoken rules like "we don't talk about that" and "that's just how Dad is."
8-inst.11: The mother who wanted to be a dancer enrolls the daughter who wants to be an engineer.
8-inst.12: The parent who abused the child claims to be the victim when the adult child sets boundaries.
8-inst.13: Families file abuse under "normal family stuff" because "every family fights."
8-inst.14: Enmeshed families discourage therapy and view friendships outside the family with suspicion.
8-inst.15: Parents pit siblings against each other until brothers and sisters see each other as rivals.
8-inst.16: Uncles, grandparents, and cousins are recruited to pressure the member who broke away.
8-inst.17: The family tells everyone that the member who left "abandoned us."
8-inst.18: Families cut members off with no fight, no conversation, and no letter, just absence.
8-inst.19: Family meetings ask the child's opinion about a decision made before the meeting started.
8-inst.20: Siblings bond over "we survived Dad together," and the shared suffering becomes the cage.
8-inst.21: Whole families shrug "this is just how our family is" and let the dysfunction continue.
8-inst.22: Families say "I'm reading your messages because I care about your safety."
8-inst.23: The youngest child is still treated as the baby of the family at forty.
8-inst.24: Families assign roles like hero child, scapegoat, and mascot so early they feel like identity.
8-inst.25: Families demand "forgiveness" before the harm has even been acknowledged.
8-inst.26: Parents use the threat of disinheritance to purchase their children's loyalty.
8-inst.27: A family health crisis surfaces the very week you planned to move out.
8-inst.28: The family member who speaks truth is permanently exiled through a withdrawal of invitations.
8-inst.29: When the golden child falls from favor, the family simply appoints a new one.
8-inst.30: Family harm spreads across a thousand micro-interactions so no single one can be blamed.

8-civ.1: Society places "family values" above the safety of the children inside the family.
8-civ.2: Culture treats a parent's self-sacrifice as a permanent moral claim on the child's obedience.
8-civ.3: Society promises marriage gets easier with time but provides no counseling to help it improve.
8-civ.4: Culture tells people abused by family "but they're your parents" to pull them back.
8-civ.5: Single parents and childless adults are spoken about in policy debates as deficiencies.
8-civ.6: A culture insists "family is everything" while millions are harmed inside their families.
8-civ.7: Culture commands children to honor parents who may be the source of their deepest wound.
8-civ.8: Culture says "family comes first" one day and "nobody owes you anything" the next.
8-civ.9: Society's ideal mother moved from stay-at-home to career woman to work-from-home supermom.
8-civ.10: Culture teaches what a good wife looks like and what a real man provides without stating it.
8-civ.11: Society blames "broken families" for dysfunction caused by overwork, poverty, and stress.
8-civ.12: Institutions that pay poverty wages and offer no parental leave blame families for failing.
8-civ.13: Generations raised inside dysfunction create the same dysfunction and call it tradition.
8-civ.14: The nuclear family replaced village child-rearing and isolated each family inside its walls.
8-civ.15: In-laws, religion, and culture are always in the room, so a married couple is never alone.
8-civ.16: Therapists and pastors ask people harmed by family, "have you considered forgiving them?"
8-civ.17: Holiday commercials and greeting cards teach that leaving your family is a moral failure.
8-civ.18: Families hold abuse as a secret for decades, believing that silence is loyalty.
8-civ.19: Society penalizes not marrying through taxes and judgment while calling marriage a free choice.
8-civ.20: Great-grandmother's silence became grandmother's anxiety, which became mother's control.
8-civ.21: Culture teaches that "you can't choose your family" so early that no one questions it.
8-civ.22: Culture insists "mother knows best" and calls the child who challenges a parent ungrateful.
8-civ.23: Culture tells adult children "they're your elders, show respect" regardless of context.
8-civ.24: Culture binds identity to the family name, status, and religion, subordinating the self.
8-civ.25: Culture says "blood is thicker than water" to put biological connection above safety.
8-civ.26: Economies require dual income while providing no subsidized childcare or paid parental leave.
8-civ.27: Cultural panic about "the decline of the family" erupts whenever marriage equality advances.
8-civ.28: Society warehouses elderly parents in understaffed nursing homes once they are not productive.
8-civ.29: Each generation discards its grandparents' wisdom as outdated and thinks it invented parenting.
8-civ.30: Culture insists "children are resilient" and "kids bounce back" to deny harm done in families.

9-inst.1: The justice system carves its claim to be fair, blind, and equal into architecture.
9-inst.2: Community policing programs build a relational debt the system can call upon for compliance.
9-inst.3: Every administration promises "criminal justice reform is coming" while cash bail remains.
9-inst.4: Prisons release people with no housing or employment and record their return as their failure.
9-inst.5: Public defenders carry sixty or eighty cases at a time, so the bank account determines justice.
9-inst.6: Prosecutors offer "two years or go to trial and risk twenty" and call the plea a choice.
9-inst.7: Communities that demand less police presence are labeled as anti-safety.
9-inst.8: Courts publicize every exoneration while thousands of appeals are denied without explanation.
9-inst.9: Mandatory minimums turn what was legal yesterday into what is criminal today.
9-inst.10: Laws hinge on terms like "reasonable suspicion" that the officer on the scene defines.
9-inst.11: The prison system gives released people nothing, then blames them for reoffending.
9-inst.12: Courts force the wrongfully convicted to prove their own innocence.
9-inst.13: American mass incarceration draws less outrage than a celebrity's social media post.
9-inst.14: Prisons remove the incarcerated from family, community, and employment for years or decades.
9-inst.15: Police, prosecutors, and judges work in the same buildings and share the same assumptions.
9-inst.16: Private prisons lobby for longer sentences to increase how many humans they are paid to cage.
9-inst.17: Defense attorneys who win high-profile cases are smeared as "getting criminals off."
9-inst.18: Police departments deny, delay, or simply ignore requests for body camera footage.
9-inst.19: Jury selection dismisses jurors who favor the defense and seats those who favor the state.
9-inst.20: Officers are bonded to a broken system by the narrative that "it's us against them."
9-inst.21: Reform-minded prosecutors burn out inside a system whose incentives oppose their work.
9-inst.22: Drug courts extend the system's reach into populations that would never have been incarcerated.
9-inst.23: Policing strategies are designed in offices that have never visited the neighborhood.
9-inst.24: The label "felon" follows a person permanently through every application and background check.
9-inst.25: Courts promise that "the verdict brings closure" when it often opens a different kind of wound.
9-inst.26: Court fines and monitoring fees compound into debt that generates warrants and more arrests.
9-inst.27: Politicians and media manufacture "crime wave" narratives to justify larger policing budgets.
9-inst.28: Departments fire or transfer officers who report corruption and keep the officers who comply.
9-inst.29: New recruits are trained in the same academy by the same instructors, so the culture holds.
9-inst.30: Police investigate police, and the internal review finds no wrongdoing.
